nodes.name: wiznet_network.c
nodes.summary: Manages WIZnet chip initialization and network lifecycle for the OPC UA USB stdio example, providing non-blocking chip bring-up, link status polling, and network status reporting.

nodes.name: wiznet_network_init
nodes.summary: Initializes the WIZnet network stack: sets up SPI, resets and initializes the chip, configures network parameters, and logs the resulting link and PHY status.

nodes.name: wiznet_network_poll
nodes.summary: Periodically polls the WIZnet PHY link status every 1 second using Pico timing, updating the internal link state.

nodes.name: wiznet_network_print_status
nodes.summary: Prints the current WIZnet network status including IP address, state name, and MAC address to stdout.

nodes.name: CMakeLists.txt
nodes.summary: CMake build configuration for the PING_TEST example, linking the example executable against the WIZnet ioLibrary and Pico SDK targets.

nodes.name: PING_TEST.c
nodes.summary: Entry-point for the PING_TEST example: initializes the WIZnet chip via SPI, configures network settings, then drives the W6300 hardware ping engine in a polling loop to send ICMP pings and report results.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Initialises SPI and WIZnet chip, configures the W6300 ping engine registers (SLRTR, SLIMR, SLCR, etc.), then loops polling SLIR to receive ping replies and report RTT.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Step-by-step guide (9 sections) covering software/hardware preparation, CMake setup for W55RP20/W6300 and generic SPI boards, build, and flashing for the PING_TEST example.

nodes.name: CMakeLists.txt
nodes.summary: CMake build configuration for the wiz_claw_agent example, linking the AI agent application against WIZnet networking and the wiz_claw library targets.

nodes.name: main.c
nodes.summary: Entry-point for the wiz_claw AI agent: initialises the Pico hardware and WIZnet Ethernet, registers a GPIO tool handler, polls a Telegram bot for incoming messages, and invokes the OpenAI-backed wiz_claw agent to dispatch tool calls controlling GPIO pins.

nodes.name: gpio_tool_handler
nodes.summary: Tool callback registered with the wiz_claw agent that parses JSON arguments to read or write Pico GPIO pins, returning the result as a JSON string.

nodes.name: on_telegram_message
nodes.summary: Telegram message callback that creates a wiz_claw agent session, runs the AI agent against the incoming message to produce a reply, then sends the response back via Telegram.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Application entry point: brings up Pico stdio/GPIO/SPI, initialises WIZnet networking and the wiz_claw network layer, registers a 1-second timer tick, and enters the main Telegram polling loop.

nodes.name: README_kr.md
nodes.summary: Korean-language README for the wiz_claw_agent example describing operation flow, network/API configuration, socket usage, GPIO tool interface, Telegram test instructions, and related files (9 sections).

nodes.name: CMakeLists.txt
nodes.summary: Top-level CMake configuration for all third-party and WIZnet libraries (ioLibrary_Driver, mbedTLS, lwIP, open62541, wiz_claw, cJSON), adding their subdirectories and defining interface targets.

nodes.name: pico_sdk_import.cmake
nodes.summary: Pico SDK CMake import helper that locates the Raspberry Pi Pico SDK from the PICO_SDK_PATH environment variable or a cached path and imports its top-level CMakeLists.

nodes.name: board_list.h
nodes.summary: Minimal header listing all supported WIZnet Pico board variants via preprocessor defines, used to select board-specific configuration at compile time.

nodes.name: can.c
nodes.summary: Complete software CAN 2.0B controller implementation (can2040) for the RP2040/RP2350, using PIO state machines for bit-level timing, hardware-accelerated bit stuffing/unstuffing, CRC computation, and interrupt-driven frame reception and transmission.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the full CAN 2.0B protocol stack in software on top of RP2040 PIO peripherals; uses GCC builtins (__builtin_clz, __builtin_bswap32) and ARM DMB memory barriers for correctness on Cortex-M0+.

nodes.name: can2040_pio_irq_handler
nodes.summary: PIO IRQ handler that dispatches incoming CAN bus events (RX data, ACK done, line matched, may-TX, TX pending) to the appropriate report handlers.

nodes.name: can2040_transmit
nodes.summary: Encodes a CAN frame (standard or extended ID, data payload) with bit stuffing and CRC into the TX queue and triggers PIO transmission.

nodes.name: can2040_start
nodes.summary: Starts the can2040 controller by resetting data state, initializing PIO hardware, and entering the initial discard state.

nodes.name: can2040_setup
nodes.summary: Initialises a can2040 state structure with a given PIO number, zeroing all fields and recording the PIO base address.

nodes.name: pio_setup
nodes.summary: Configures all four PIO state machines (sync, RX, match, TX) for CAN bus timing, sets clock dividers, and assigns GPIO pins to PIO functions.

nodes.name: process_rx
nodes.summary: Processes a raw PIO RX word by feeding bits through the unstuffer and data state machine, handling passive and error conditions.

nodes.name: can.h
nodes.summary: Public header for the can2040 software CAN controller, declaring the can2040 state struct, can2040_msg frame type, statistics struct, and the public API (setup, start, stop, transmit, check_transmit, callback_config, get_statistics, pio_irq_handler).

nodes.name: can.pio
nodes.summary: RP2040 PIO assembly programs (sync, RX, match, TX state machines) implementing the low-level CAN bus bit sampling, matching, and transmission timing used by can2040.
nodes.languageNotes: PIO assembly for the RP2040 programmable I/O subsystem; each program handles a specific phase of the CAN protocol (sync detection, bit reception, frame matching, bit transmission).

nodes.name: CMakeLists.txt
nodes.summary: CMake configuration for the port layer, defining the wizchip_spi, wizchip_qspi_pio, wizchip_gpio_irq, and CAN library targets with their sources, include paths, and Pico SDK dependencies.

nodes.name: wizchip_gpio_irq.h
nodes.summary: Header declaring the GPIO interrupt initialization function and the user-configurable callback pointer for WIZnet chip interrupt handling.

nodes.name: wizchip_qspi_pio.h
nodes.summary: Header for the QSPI PIO driver, declaring the SPI configuration structure, handle type, and the open/close/frame/register functions for WIZnet QSPI communication via RP2040 PIO.

nodes.name: wizchip_spi.h
nodes.summary: Main port header declaring WIZnet SPI initialization, chip reset, network initialization, and information-printing functions, plus network info and status structures used across all examples.

nodes.name: wizchip_gpio_irq.c
nodes.summary: Implements GPIO interrupt support for the WIZnet chip, configuring socket interrupt masks and attaching a user-supplied callback to the interrupt GPIO.

nodes.name: wizchip_gpio_interrupt_initialize
nodes.summary: Enables per-socket interrupt masks on the WIZnet chip and registers the GPIO falling-edge callback with the Pico SDK IRQ system.
